probe.oracle_gap: The probe models ONLY the transform containing-block mechanism. It passes while the real app still fails because the remaining trap is a STACKING CONTEXT from the body's active opacity animation, which the probe does not model.

root_cause_proven.confirmation: Runtime DOM probe in the rebuilt app: temporarily setting animation:none on #context-panel-outline-body makes the menu hit-testable (elementFromPoint returns the menu); restoring it re-traps the menu.
root_cause_proven.mechanism: The active tf-anim-materialize animation (fill-mode:both) on .context-panel-outline-body creates a stacking context in Chromium even though the keyframe is opacity-only and computed transform is 'none'. The position:fixed row menu / retarget popover are trapped in that context, which paints beneath .workspace-main, so they are occluded and unclickable wherever they extend past the navigator into the document area.
root_cause_proven.tfl1080_hypothesis: FALSE - 'opacity-only keyframe removes the containing block' does not hold; the animation itself (not transform) still traps fixed descendants.
